chemistry-killer-02.title: Mixtures and Dissolution Principles (2)
chemistry-killer-02.goal: Analyze the principles of Mixtures and Dissolution Principles (2) and deduce the correct conclusion under given conditions.
chemistry-killer-02.material:
At constant temperature and pressure, hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) reacts with oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) to form water vapor ($\mathrm{H_2O}$(g)). Different gas mixtures were reacted completely and the total gas volume was measured at the same temperature and pressure (all water is gaseous).
(A) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 30 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL -> total 35 mL after reaction
(B) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 20 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL -> total 30 mL after reaction
A 60 mL mixture of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ was reacted completely at the same temperature and pressure. The total volume after reaction was 45 mL and the only gas left over was $\mathrm{O_2}$ (no $\mathrm{H_2}$ left). Which pair correctly gives the volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ before reaction and the volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ left after reaction, in that order?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.prompt:
At constant temperature and pressure, hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) reacts with oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) to form water vapor ($\mathrm{H_2O}$(g)). Different gas mixtures were reacted completely and the total gas volume was measured at the same temperature and pressure (all water is gaseous).
(A) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 30 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL -> total 35 mL after reaction
(B) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 20 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL -> total 30 mL after reaction
A 60 mL mixture of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ was reacted completely at the same temperature and pressure. The total volume after reaction was 45 mL and the only gas left over was $\mathrm{O_2}$ (no $\mathrm{H_2}$ left). Which pair correctly gives the volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ before reaction and the volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ left after reaction, in that order?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: From (A) and (B) the volume ratio. (B): 20 mL of H2 reacts with 10 mL of O2 to give 20 mL of H2O, 10 mL of O2 left, total 30 mL. (A): 30 mL of H2 reacts with 15 mL of O2 to give 30 mL of H2O, 5 mL of O2 left, total 35 mL. So $\mathrm{H_2:O_2:H_2O(g)} = 2:1:2$.
Step 2: Volume falls from 60 mL to 45 mL, a decrease of 15 mL. Each reaction of 3 volumes into 2 loses 1 volume, equal to the O2 volume reacted, so O2 reacted = 15 mL.
Step 3: No H2 is left, so H2 reacted = 15 x 2 = 30 mL, H2O(g) = 30 mL. Total after = 45 mL, so O2 left = 45 - 30 = 15 mL. Initial O2 = 15 + 15 = 30 mL, and 30 + 30 = 60 mL checks out.
Answer: 30 mL, 15 mL (b).
chemistry-killer-02.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.hint.0: In $\mathrm{2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O(g)}$, 3 volumes of gas become 2 volumes, so the decrease in volume equals the volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ that reacted.
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.hint.1: Decrease = 60 - 45 = 15 mL = $\mathrm{O_2}$ reacted. All the $\mathrm{H_2}$ reacted, so $\mathrm{H_2}$ = 15 x 2 = 30 mL and $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$ formed = 30 mL.
